case_studies.title: The Ethics of Autonomous AI Agents for Offensive Security
case_studies.abstract: LLM-driven autonomous agents are reshaping offensive security. Unlike traditional penetration-testing tooling -- deterministic, narrowly scoped, and operated by trained practitioners -- agentic security tools exhibit \textit{indeterminacy} along three independent dimensions. First, their actions are drawn from a non-deterministic policy whose outputs resist both ex-ante and ex-post explanation, frustrating incident attribution and pre-deployment safety review. Second, their impact is open-ended due to the non-deterministic actions, agency of utilized models, and opaque LLM supply-chains. Third
case_studies.summary: This research explores the ethics of using autonomous AI agents for offensive security, which can pose risks due to their unpredictable actions and impact. The authors studied the use of Large Language Model (LLM)-driven autonomous agents in security testing. The result highlights the potential risks and challenges of using such agents in security testing.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud security infrastructure, this flags a risk: if your organization uses autonomous AI agents for penetration testing, check their explainability and safety review processes immediately. This is particularly relevant if you use LLM-driven tools. Review your incident attribution processes to ensure you can identify and respond to potential security incidents.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: 20 (indeterminacy of LLM-driven agents) + 5 (autonomous AI) = 25. IT Relevance: 20 (agentic security tools for offense) + 5 (LLM policy) = 25. Value 90 days: 20 (identify non-deterministic actions and impact) + 5 (suggest risk flags or mitigation strategies) = 25 (rounded to 20 for specific suggestions).

case_studies.title: HiMe: Real-Time Self-Hosted Personal Agent Platform for Health Insights with Wearable Devices
case_studies.abstract: Traditional approaches to wearable health signal analysis, such as smartwatches, are constrained by rigid analytical frameworks and limited personalisation. The emergence of LLM agents creates a new opportunity for Personal Health Agentic Analysis, where health insights can be generated adaptively and in context. However, currently there is no open-source locally deployable platform capable of processing personal health data in real time while preserving privacy. We present HiMe, a locally deployable, privacy-first agent platform that is fully compatible with real-time health data ecosystems a
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of limited personalisation in wearable health signal analysis by building a real-time self-hosted personal agent platform called HiMe. HiMe allows for adaptive and contextual health insights while preserving user privacy. The result is a locally deployable platform that can process personal health data in real time.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage health-related cloud infrastructure, here is what to do: assess your current data processing capabilities for wearable devices, check if your organisation uses rigid analytical frameworks, and consider HiMe as an alternative for real-time health data ecosystems. This flags a risk: if your org uses wearable devices for health analysis, check your current data processing for potential privacy vulnerabilities immediately. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work outside of health-related systems.
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper presents HiMe, a locally deployable platform for personal health agentic analysis. This directly relates to IT engineers and consultants working on IT infrastructure. While not novel to IT experts, it could be valuable for them working with healthcare clients or on projects integrating wearable devices. case_studies.title: From Resource Flow to Executable Tests: Petri-Net-Guided LLM Test Generation for Concurrent Stateful Rust APIs
case_studies.abstract: Concurrent stateful library APIs expose behavior through evolving resource ownership, lifecycle states, and competing interleavings. Large language models can synthesize executable Rust tests, but their outputs often violate API preconditions, remain shallow, or reduce concurrency to accidental sequential traces. Conversely, model-based and systematic testing techniques provide semantic control but commonly require substantial handwritten code to turn abstract scenarios into executable tests. This paper addresses the gap between formal scenario design and low-cost test concretization. We prese
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of generating executable tests for concurrent stateful APIs, the authors built a system that uses Petri-Nets to guide large language models to generate tests, and the result is more effective and efficient test generation. This could impact IT work related to testing and quality assurance. The research focuses on Rust APIs and concurrent systems.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage Rust-based APIs or concurrent systems, here is what to do: review your current testing approach, consider integrating Petri-Net-guided large language models to improve test generation, and evaluate the potential benefits for your organization's testing efficiency and effectiveness.
case_studies.score_reasoning: IT engineers can benefit from learning about LLM test generation in Rust APIs, but direct applicability is limited. The novelty of Petri-Net-Guided approach is moderate, and the ability to automate test generation within 90 days is good (but not applicable in most real-world settings).

case_studies.title: Toward Continuous Assurance for the Democratization of AI Agent Creation in Industry
case_studies.abstract: AI agents are increasingly created inside organizations by non-engineering users through low-code, no-code, and conversational development environments. This democratization enables rapid local innovation, but it also creates a reliability gap: agents that appear to users as simple productivity artifacts may depend on changing models, tools, retrieval sources, permissions, prompts, schedules, and external services. These dependencies can cause silent degradation long after deployment, even when no user directly modifies the agent. This paper identifies the reliability challenge created by demo
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of reliability gaps in AI agents created by non-engineering users, by identifying the challenges of dependencies on changing models and external services, and the authors built a framework for continuous assurance. The result is a better understanding of the potential for silent degradation in AI agents. This affects IT work as it highlights the need for monitoring and maintenance of AI agents in cloud infrastructure.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure that uses low-code or no-code AI agents, here is what to do: step 1, review the dependencies of these agents, step 2, implement monitoring for silent degradation, step 3, update maintenance schedules to include these agents.
case_studies.score_reasoning: High relevance due to AI deployment and agentic systems. Moderate novelty.

case_studies.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
case_studies.abstract: Unlike large language models (LLMs) that exhibit strong reasoning capabilities, vision-language models (VLMs) struggle with visual reasoning, even on geometry problems that admit equivalent text, diagram, and combined diagram+text views. We show that these views often elicit different behaviors: a model may solve a problem from text but fail on the corresponding diagram, or succeed visually while failing textually. This inconsistency suggests that different views expose complementary reasoning paths and failure modes that standard multimodal post-training does not fully exploit. To study and e
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of vision-language models struggling with visual reasoning by building a system called MIRROR that learns from different views of a problem. The result is a model that can exploit complementary reasoning paths and failure modes. It does not directly impact IT infrastructure work.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on improving vision-language models for multi-modal reasoning tasks.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper proposes a research project with potential for real-world application, but novelty is mostly limited to academic NLP context. Although relevant to language models, it is not directly applicable to IT infrastructure, software engineering, AI deployment, or automation. Value over next 90 days is limited to theoretical understanding, but not a clear path to building or automating something.

case_studies.title: Where You Tap Matters: A Probe-and-Model Benchmark for Open-Set RF Fingerprinting
case_studies.abstract: Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification (RFFI) enables transmitter identification at the physical layer by learning device-specific impairments from received signals, yet the literature is inconsistent about where in the receiver chain those samples should be collected. Since distinct transformations are applied to the signal by the different receiver operations, i.e., carrier recovery, gain normalization, pulse shaping, and timing recovery, they can either tighten within-transmitter variability or suppress the features RFFI requires for classification. We present a systematic real-world ev
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inconsistent results in Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification by determining the best point in the receiver chain to collect signal samples. The team built a benchmark to test the effectiveness of different sample collection points. The result is a clearer understanding of how to improve transmitter identification at the physical layer.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on radio frequency signal processing and transmitter identification at the physical layer.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Medium novelty and relevance due to AI research on a specific domain, but no clear indication of its value to IT engineers or consultants in the UK.

case_studies.title: Diffusion Language Model for Recommendation
case_studies.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-empowered recommender systems have emerged as a promising paradigm for generative recommendation, leveraging their strong semantic reasoning and generative capacity to model complex, diverse user preferences. However, most existing approaches rely on an autoregressive paradigm that is suboptimal for recommendation. The next-token objective emphasizes sequential order rather than the structural inter-item dependencies underlying user preferences. In addition, prefix-constrained generation restricts bidirectional context and commits to left-to-right decoding, causing e
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inefficient recommendation systems by building a diffusion language model that better captures user preferences. The result is a more effective generative recommendation system. This is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on improving recommendation systems rather than cloud management.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novel use case of large language models in recommendation systems with potential applications, but mostly relevant to academia.

case_studies.title: PATS: Policy-Aware Training Scaffolding for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
case_studies.abstract: In long-horizon LLM agent reinforcement learning, weak policies often repeat similar failures, producing uninformative rollout trajectories and limiting effective policy optimization. Existing skill-centric methods improve exploration by optimizing, filtering, or internalizing reusable skills. However, they remain centered on the skills themselves rather than being designed as adaptive training-time support for the evolving policy. To address this, we propose a policy-centric training paradigm that reframes skills as a dynamic training scaffold. Our framework, Pats, converts rollout groups fro
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of weak policies in reinforcement learning by building a policy-centric training framework called PATS, which reframes skills as a dynamic training scaffold. The result is improved exploration and policy optimization in long-horizon reinforcement learning. This is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on reinforcement learning and policy optimization in artificial intelligence.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: 10 - The concept of a policy-centric training scaffold for LLM agents may be new to IT engineers, although the context is academic. Relevance: 5 - The focus is on LLM agents, a topic relevant to IT but not as directly impactful as other aspects of AI. Value: 30 - The framework might be used to improve AI model training, but this could take significant time and resources, and there's no immediate, direct application to IT infrastructure.

case_studies.title: Agentic coding without the cloud: evaluating open-weight large language models on longitudinal data preparation tasks
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) and agents are now widely used tools in code development, with data typically sent to third-party cloud-based models. Their adoption in research using personal data is constrained by governance requirements that typically prohibit data transmission to external services. Locally deployable open-weight models offer an alternative since sensitive data never leave the local environment. We introduce an open-source framework for evaluating the efficacy of AI agents powered by open-weight LLMs on one of the most persistent bottlenecks in research on longitudinal populati
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of using large language models with sensitive data by building a locally deployable open-weight model, which allows data to be processed without being sent to the cloud. The result is an open-source framework for evaluating the efficacy of AI agents powered by these models. This framework can help with data preparation tasks in research on longitudinal population studies.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure for research institutions, here is what to do: assess the use of sensitive data in your cloud deployments, consider deploying open-weight large language models locally to avoid data transmission to external services, and evaluate the new open-source framework for potential integration.
case_studies.score_reasoning: While the idea of open-weight large language models is interesting, the application of this research to IT infrastructure is limited. The novelty lies in the open-source framework, but its relevance to IT engineers is low as it focuses on longitudinal data preparation tasks and AI agents without direct implications for tools or systems they use. The value within 90 days is non-existent.
